properties.name: The hosted surface is READ-ONLY, which is what lets it ship before authentication exists — refusing writes bounds the exposure to confidentiality, and the tailnet bounds that
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-26, choosing the first cut of `dec:central-host` option (c) after the write question was put to him: **read-only surface first, writes deferred.**

📌 Distinct from `dec:central-host`, which the duplicate guard offered and which was read before choosing: that node decides WHICH ROAD among four; this states WHAT MUST BE TRUE of the first cut, and is the thing a capability will satisfy.

═══ WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED ═══

Option (c)'s cheapest cut is far smaller than the decision implied, because two of its three pieces already ship:

    TRANSPORT            BUILT     `--http <ADDR>`; `cap:shared-sessions` verified,
                                   `ver:shared-sessions` passing over real HTTP
    CROSS-MACHINE REACH  BUILT     `--http-allow-host <HOST>`; `cap:remote-sessions` VERIFIED,
                                   `req:sessions-across-machines` ACCEPTED. Extends the default
                                   allowlist rather than replacing it, and warns when a
                                   non-loopback bind names no host
    AUTHENTICATION       ABSENT    none, at all

So a session on another machine can attach to a shared reflow2 today. What has never existed is any answer to *who is calling*.

═══ ⭐ THE ARGUMENT: READ-ONLY IS WHAT MAKES THE MISSING AUTHENTICATION SURVIVABLE ═══

`cap:remote-sessions` states the exposure in its own words: the Host allowlist is *"DNS-rebinding protection, and with no authentication on reflow2 it is the only thing between a web page the user visits and their design."*

**A read-only surface splits that exposure in two and answers one half outright.**

- **INTEGRITY** — can a reacher CORRUPT the design? On a read-only surface, no. There is no write to attribute, so `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` (ENFORCED) is untouched, and the caller-supplied `contributor_id` that would otherwise be an unverified claim over a network is never accepted.
- **CONFIDENTIALITY** — can a reacher SEE the design? Yes, and nothing in reflow2 prevents it. **This is the residual risk; it is not eliminated, it is relocated to the network** — which is what option (c)'s tailnet binding is for, and why the binding belongs in the requirement rather than in an implementation note.

⇒ **Read-only + tailnet is shippable WITHOUT building authentication at all.** That is the whole reason for this ordering, and it must not be read as authentication being unnecessary — only as it not blocking the first cut.

═══ WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DELIVER ═══

⚠️ **A web-app user can SEE the design and cannot CONTRIBUTE to it.** That is less than the 2026-08-11 flo2 case asked for, which was a user POSTING a brainstormed idea. The gap is known, chosen, and named here so nobody reads the shipped surface as answering flo2 in full.

📌 **THE ATTRIBUTION PASS-THROUGH IS DEFERRED, NOT SOLVED**, and remains open on `dec:central-host`. It becomes the blocking question the moment writes are wanted. Its shape is probably already designed: `dec:stateless-seat-handle` (ACCEPTED, unbuilt) settled MINT-AND-CARRY for seats — a server-minted handle passed as an ordinary tool argument, with a REFUSAL rather than a guess when it is missing — and explicitly rejected deriving identity from request headers as trading *"a loud missing parameter for a quiet wrong answer"*. Attribution needs that same shape for a different question: a seat says WHICH SESSION, a contributor says WHOSE WORD.

🛑 AND THE HARD PART THAT SHAPE DOES NOT SOLVE: today `authored_by` validates only that the Contributor EXISTS (`require_contributor`), never that the caller IS them. Locally that is sound, because the trust boundary is the machine. Over a network it makes attribution and AUTHORISATION the same field, and reflow2 has never had to tell them apart.
